title: Characteristic-zero DVR completion is a regular map
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local discrete valuation ring, that is, a Noetherian local domain of Krull dimension one whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is principal (Stacks Algebra, Lemma Tag 00PD), and assume that its fraction field $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ has characteristic zero. Let $A^\wedge=\varprojlim_nA/\mathfrak m^n$ be its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion, with the canonical ring map $A\to A^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then $A\to A^\wedge$ is a regular ring map in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition Tag 07PX (proposition-ubiquity-G-ring), proof of item (3), in the characteristic-zero DVR case: the completion is a DVR by More on Algebra Lemma Tag 0AP1 (lemma-completion-dvr), completion is flat by Algebra Lemma Tag 00MB (lemma-completion-flat), and the generic and closed fibres are geometrically regular; the Noetherian local-domain, dimension-one, principal-maximal-ideal characterization is Algebra Lemma Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), and regular ring maps are Definition Tag 07BZ.

proof.text: Notation and flatness. Write $\iota:A\to A^\wedge$ for the canonical map. Since $A$ has Krull dimension one, $\mathfrak m\neq0$ (otherwise $(0)$ would be the only prime ideal and the dimension would be $0$); so $\mathfrak m=\pi A$ for a nonzero $\pi\in A$, and $A$ satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power]. As $A$ is Noetherian, $\iota$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat] (with $I=\mathfrak m$). This is the flatness half of the definition of a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]; it remains to check that every fibre $A^\wedge\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: More on Algebra 07PX proof ('from the definition'); flatness: Algebra Lemma Tag 00MB (lemma-completion-flat)

proof.text: The primes of $A$ are $(0)$ and $\mathfrak m$. $(0)$ is prime as $A$ is a domain, and $\mathfrak m$ is prime. Let $\mathfrak p\neq0$ be a prime and $0\neq x\in\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], $x=u\pi^n$ with $u$ a unit, so $\pi^n=u^{-1}x\in\mathfrak p$, hence $\pi\in\mathfrak p$ ($\mathfrak p$ prime; $n\ge1$ since $\mathfrak p$ contains no unit), so $\mathfrak m=\pi A\subseteq\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m$ (every proper ideal of the local ring $A$ lies in $\mathfrak m$), i.e. $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Algebra Lemma Tag 00PD (every nonzero element is u pi^n); written out by the agent

proof.text: The completion. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-of-dvr-is-dvr], $A^\wedge$ is a Noetherian local domain whose maximal ideal is generated by a single nonzero element. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak mA^\wedge$, the ideal generated by $\iota(\mathfrak m)=\iota(\pi)\iota(A)$, i.e. $\mathfrak mA^\wedge=\iota(\pi)A^\wedge$; and $\iota(\pi)\neq0$, since otherwise this maximal ideal would be $0$, while it is generated by a nonzero element. So $A^\wedge$ with the generator $\iota(\pi)$ satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power]: every nonzero $b\in A^\wedge$ is $v\,\iota(\pi)^n$ with $v$ a unit of $A^\wedge$.

source.place: More on Algebra Lemma Tag 0AP1 (lemma-completion-dvr), as cited in the proof of 07PX

source.place: More on Algebra 07PX proof (generic fibre); written out by the agent

proof.text: The generic fibre is geometrically regular over $K$. Let $K'/K$ be a finite purely inseparable extension. Since $K$ has characteristic zero, $K'=K$ by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] (the characteristic-zero clause: the structure map $K\to K'$ is an isomorphism). Hence $K'\otimes_KL\cong K\otimes_KL\cong L$, a field, and a field is a regular ring by [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring] (regularity passes along a ring isomorphism). So $L$ is geometrically regular over $K=\kappa((0))$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: More on Algebra 07PX proof ('fraction field of characteristic zero'); written out by the agent

proof.text: The closed fibre. Since $A$ is local, $A\setminus\mathfrak m=A^\times$, so $A\to A_{\mathfrak m}$ is an isomorphism and $k:=\kappa(\mathfrak m)=A_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak mA_{\mathfrak m}=A/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] (1) with $J=\mathfrak m$, $M=A^\wedge$, $A^\wedge\otimes_A A/\mathfrak m\cong A^\wedge/\mathfrak mA^\wedge$, $b\otimes\bar a\mapsto \iota(a)b\bmod\mathfrak mA^\wedge$, a ring isomorphism under which the $k$-algebra structure $\bar a\mapsto1\otimes\bar a$ becomes the map $A/\mathfrak m\to A^\wedge/\mathfrak mA^\wedge$ induced by $\iota$. That map is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]. So the fibre over $\mathfrak m$ is isomorphic, as a $k$-algebra, to $k$ itself: a field, Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring]. For every finite purely inseparable $k'/k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], $k'\otimes_k k\cong k'$ is a field, hence regular by [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring]. So the closed fibre is geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: More on Algebra 07PX proof (closed fibre A^/mA^ = A/m); Algebra Lemma Tag 05GG via the node

proof.text: Conclusion. $\iota$ is flat (step 1), the primes of $A$ are $(0)$ and $\mathfrak m$ (step 2), and the fibres over them are Noetherian and geometrically regular over the residue fields (steps 4-6). By the definition of a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], $A\to A^\wedge$ is regular.
